pilotFactors: Well rested, current, and in good physical condition
Fatigued from a late night (reduced alertness)
Distracted by personal concerns (e.g., recent family issue)
Under stress from a recent financial concern
aircraftFactors: Properly maintained and fully equipped aircraft
Recently serviced with updated avionics (slightly unfamiliar)
Equipped for VFR only (no IFR capability)
environmentalFactors: Unfamiliar airspace along route of flight or at the destination
externalPressures: Passenger has a tight schedule and requests an early arrival
Client expects delivery of urgent medical supplies by a deadline
Family member awaiting your arrival for an important event
Pressure to complete the flight to meet a personal commitment
Desire to prove your skills to a mentor or instructor
difficultyAdjustment: Private Pilot: Scenarios and questions are straightforward, testing baseline aeronautical knowledge, fundamental airmanship, and risk management under Part 61 and Part 91 for VFR operations.

Instrument Rating: Scenarios and questions test IFR operations with moderate challenges, requiring intermediate aeronautical knowledge, precise airmanship, and risk management under Part 61 and Part 91.

Commercial Pilot: Scenarios and questions involve nuanced for-hire operations, testing greater depth in aeronautical knowledge, enhanced airmanship, and risk management under Part 61, Part 91, and Part 119/135 with increased analytical complexity.

Airline Transport Pilot (ATP): Scenarios and questions test complex operations, requiring comprehensive aeronautical knowledge, advanced airmanship, crew coordination, and risk management under Part 61, Part 91, and Part 121/135 with complex conditions.
